title: An A-module on a scheme with quasi-coherent algebra A is quasi-coherent over A exactly when it is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf

standard_prerequisites.name: Local presentations of a quasi-coherent module as the cokernel of a map of direct sums of the structure sheaf or of the algebra, on an open neighbourhood of a point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: This is what the two directions of the proof use at proof lines 2074-2078 and 2095-2102
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequences in terms of which the module is recognised as quasi-coherent over the algebra, respectively over the structure sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The tilde construction over an affine scheme: a quasi-coherent algebra on Spec(R) is the tilde of an R-algebra, a quasi-coherent module is the tilde of an R-module, and the tilde functor is exact
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 2086-2092 and again at 2103-2108
standard_prerequisites.use: Translates the second direction into a statement about an R-algebra A and an R-module M with an A-module structure, and transfers an A-module presentation back to sheaves.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cokernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme are quasi-coherent, and exactness of a sequence of modules over an algebra regarded as a sequence of modules over the smaller ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Closes the first direction and identifies the compatible structures in the affine chart.

core_obligations: First direction: for an A-module F that is quasi-coherent as an A-module, use at each point the local presentation of F as a cokernel of a map of direct sums of A restricted to an open neighbourhood, regard the same exact sequence as a sequence of modules over the structure sheaf, and conclude that F restricted to that neighbourhood is a cokernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules, hence that F is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf (proof lines 2072-2081).

Second direction, affine chart: assume F is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf and pick an open affine U = Spec(R); identify the algebra restricted to U with the tilde of an R-algebra A and F restricted to U with the tilde of an R-module M, so that the A-module structure on F becomes an A-module structure on M compatible with the R-module structure (proof lines 2081-2094).

Choose a presentation of M as the cokernel of a map of direct sums of A, and use exactness of the tilde functor to turn it into a presentation of F restricted to U as the cokernel of a map of direct sums of the tilde of A, which says exactly that F is quasi-coherent as an A-module (proof lines 2095-2108).
proof_roadmap: One direction transfers a local A-module presentation to the structure sheaf and reads quasi-coherence off a cokernel (proof lines 2072-2081).

The other direction goes to an affine chart, turns the algebra and the module into their algebraic counterparts, and transfers an A-module presentation back through the exact tilde functor (proof lines 2081-2108).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the scalar-restriction lemma for a quasi-coherent algebra A on a scheme: an A-module is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf exactly when it is quasi-coherent over A (statement lines 2061-2070). The counted proof does both directions concretely: the first reads quasi-coherence over the structure sheaf off a local A-module presentation regarded over the smaller sheaf of rings, and the second descends to an affine chart, where the algebra and the module become an R-algebra A and an R-module M with an A-module structure, and then transfers a presentation of M over A back to a presentation of the sheaf over the tilde of A using exactness of the tilde functor (proof lines 2072-2108). It is H2: the argument is complete and self-contained and the only input is the standard local presentation of quasi-coherent modules, so no H3 claim is made.
